wayland_sync_review:
# H9 Wayland sync and release audit

## Hardware prerequisite

`s5-wayland-baseline-default.log` records a successful GNOME Wayland run of the Pelt `--wayland-present-smoke` route: 800×600, 60 frames, `created_window=true`, `declared_subsurface=false`, exit status 0. The smoke clears the prior `PresentationOutcome` before each render and accepts a frame only after a fresh `DisplayHandoff` (`mere/ports/pelt/desktop/smoke_wayland.rs:339-356`). The pre-cut compositor source hashes are in `s5-wayland-baseline-compositor-sha256.json`. This run exercises repeated master-buffer presentation and slot reuse; it does not exercise the declared-subsurface or baked paths, nor establish pixel correctness.

## Queue custody

The smoke creates one Vulkan `wgpu::Device` and `wgpu::Queue` pair, puts them in `WgpuHandles`, clones that same pair for `HostWgpuContext`, and moves the original handles into netrender (`mere/ports/pelt/desktop/smoke_wayland.rs:190-209,240-262`). At the pinned netrender revision `e8cda06efc11c11595f2fa1bb30bce7e72979537`, `create_netrender_instance` consumes `WgpuHandles` into `WgpuDevice::with_external` (`netrender/src/renderer/init.rs:105-130`). The compositor render path calls the rasterizer and passes its handles to `present_frame` (`netrender/src/renderer/mod.rs:1243-1256,1342-1355`); the Vello rasterizer renders on `&self.handles.queue` (`netrender/src/vello_tile_rasterizer/mod.rs:598-613`). The Wayland backend clones the supplied host context (`genet/components/genet-compositor/compositor_wayland/mod.rs:159-174`) and submits master and child copies through `self.host.queue` (`:277-303`, `:441-467`), with the bake path also taking `&self.host.queue` (`:618-625`). Thus this supported Pelt route uses one queue for producer and consumer submissions. `SyncMechanism::None` reflects that caller contract (`:691-694`); the constructor does not prove queue identity for arbitrary embedders and no cross-queue handshake is offered.

## Slot custody and release

`allocate_pool` constructs two slots per pool (`genet/components/genet-compositor/compositor_wayland/mod.rs:182-191`). Each `wl_buffer` carries `BufferSlotUserData` with an `Arc<Mutex<bool>>` shared with its slot (`:194-245`; `dmabuf.rs:428-450`). `SurfaceBufferPool::acquire` marks an available slot in flight and refuses both busy slots (`dmabuf.rs:452-465`). The master path dispatches pending Wayland events before acquisition, then roundtrips while both slots are busy (`mod.rs:249-275`). The Wayland `wl_buffer.release` dispatcher clears that exact slot's flag (`wayland.rs:317-333`). Child fast and baked paths use the same acquire/roundtrip pattern (`mod.rs:405-433,590-601`). Their native submit, attach, commit, and flush paths remain unchanged. The 60-frame hardware pass is practical evidence that the master pool released and reused slots; child reuse remains source-supported but not hardware-qualified by this baseline.

## Cut and validation boundary

The only `WaylandSubsurfaceBackend` timeline use was a stored `VulkanTimelineSemaphoreSynchronizer` initialized in `new`, never signaled, waited on, or read. Removed its import, field, construction, and now-unused `BackendError::SyncInit` case in `compositor_wayland/mod.rs` and `compositor_wayland/errors.rs`. The reusable `interop/vulkan_timeline.rs` primitive and export remain for a future multi-queue consumer. No queue, pool, release, or native backend behavior was changed. Static search finds no remaining Wayland timeline or `SyncInit` references; `git diff --check` passes. The controller owns post-cut compile, unit, and hardware rerun.
